answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds impose staking collateral S whose withdrawal incurs a subgame-perfect slashing penalty λ>S, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay τ lengthens the payoff horizon; thus any identity multiplication yields expected utility E[U]=p·r−λ·(1−p)−c·τ<0, proving strict negative attack utility.
